R760.note: unique_ptr moved into a shared_ptr captured by value; the queued callback now owns the Session, exactly one callback is enqueued, and the removal of session.reset() is stated and required by the contract.

R761.note: WebUtility.HtmlEncode wraps only the tainted value in a Web Forms Response.Write body context; null input still concatenates as empty, static markup unchanged.

R762.note: Magic-number sniffing replaces the client Content-Type check and derives the extension from verified bytes, but the added 5 MB MaxAvatarBytes cap is a new restriction the original never had and can reject a legitimate larger upload, even though it is stated.

R763.note: JsonSerializer.Serialize with the default encoder escapes quotes, backslashes, and <>&' as \uXXXX so the value is safe as a JS string literal and cannot close the script element; Title encoding and the numeric refreshSeconds are untouched, satisfying the contract.

R764.note: RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(32) hex-encoded via Convert.ToHexString gives 256 bits of CSPRNG output; the token format change (36-char GUID to 64-char hex) is stated plainly and the dictionary/response types are unchanged.

R765.note: HMAC-prefix verification only works if the nightly batch job (explicitly out of scope) starts signing, so it is the wrong shape here versus a restricted Unpickler with a find_class allowlist; as applied, every existing plain-pickle cache entry now raises ValueError (500) and the write-up frames the job as already signing rather than stating the producer change as a required follow-up, plus os.environ[...] makes import fail if the key is unset.

R766.note: In-handler socket.user.role check sourced from the verified JWT closes the missing per-event authorization; non-admins fall through to the same silent return the handler already uses for bad payloads, and nothing else changes.

R767.note: ECB replaced by CBC with a fresh GenerateIV() per call and the IV prepended to the returned ciphertext; the changed output layout is inherent to leaving ECB and is stated plainly with the decryption offset, hardcoded key correctly noted as out of scope.

R768.note: Rejecting CR/LF in the filename before the socket is opened is the exact neutralization for FTP control-channel injection and only refuses values that cannot be a legitimate single RETR argument; the write-up's 'documented below' has no matching section but the IllegalArgumentException change is stated inline.

R769.note: setObjectInputFilter with 'evalcases.OrderEvent;java.base/*;!*' keeps the native wire format the out-of-scope publisher uses and rejects unlisted classes before construction; InvalidClassException still surfaces through the existing RuntimeException wrapper, and the caveat about other in-repo field types is stated.

R770.note: node-serialize's own output is JSON plus eval'd function markers, so JSON.parse reads every legitimate profile cookie while removing the eval path; the plain-object guard is stated, and a malformed cookie now yields {} (same as the existing no-cookie path) instead of throwing, which blocks no legitimate caller.

R771.note: The regex allowlist does keep CR/LF out of docmd(), but it is stricter than the envelope-address contract: it rejects quoted local parts, IP-literal and dotless domains, and the empty string the original's own default produced as the legitimate null sender MAIL FROM:<>, so it refuses inputs the original accepted even though the write-up states it.

R772.note: jwt.decode now takes the env-provisioned secret with algorithms pinned to HS256, and PyJWTError maps to the same 401 shape the function already used for a missing header; the HS256 assumption and the JWT_SECRET_KEY deployment requirement are both stated.

R773.note: Parameterizing both values with typed SqlParameters closes the injection and preserves the string-to-datetime comparison and null handling, but the unstated NVarChar sizes (100 and 50) make SqlClient silently truncate longer inputs before the DELETE, a new bound the write-up never mentions.
